chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Humran, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Al-mubar'ah (separation of the marital bond) becomes clear from that moment without a formal divorce, and there is no inheritance between them, because the 'ismah (bond of marriage) has separated from them at the moment that condition occurred from her and from the husband.'

key_terms.الْعِصْمَةَ: Al-'ismah: Here referring to the bond or tie of marriage (as 'ismah can mean bond/tie in this context, distinct from infallibility).
key_terms.الْمُبَارَأَةُ: Al-mubar'ah: Separation of the marital bond, a specific legal mechanism in Shia fiqh where the bond is severed by a condition or act without formal divorce.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Mubar'ah regarding divorce and inheritance in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that 'al-mubar'ah' (mutual separation by agreement) effects an immediate, irrevocable severance of the marital bond without requiring a formal 'talaq', thereby instantly terminating inheritance rights. This ruling highlights the distinct Shia jurisprudential view that the marital contract can be dissolved by mutual consent alone, emphasizing the concept of ''israh' (severance) as the operative legal mechanism rather than the procedural act of divorce.
